mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over three consecutive months signals a monetary easing cycle, which reduces the cost of capital and boosts equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS falls by at least 50 basis points over three months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than baseline during triggered episodes (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained acceleration in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1 growth) above 3% quarter-over-quarter signals stronger economic demand, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 q/q growth > 3% for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 8.5% within a month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depress consumer spending and corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 8.5% in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 95 for two consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during triggered periods (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both real personal income (PAYEMS) and consumer spending (proxied by RSAFS) signals robust household demand, which boosts corporate revenues and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and RSAFS both increase month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when both proxies co-move upward (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and a decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) over two months signals a successful disinflationary tightening, which initially depresses markets but ultimately supports long-term returns, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls in the same two-month window
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly above baseline during episodes of simultaneous rate hikes and falling inflation (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as profit margins compress.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of extreme labor market tightness (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained drop in housing starts (HOUST) below 500K units for four consecutive months signals a housing market downturn, which negatively impacts construction and related industries and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during triggered housing downturns (p > 0.10).
